The evidence, and why it is paper only
Tested on NSE 2005–2020, data it had never seen, with its rules fixed first: 33,979 trades, +0.21% a trade after futures charges, t 4.66, positive in every 5-year period but shrinking (+0.40%, +0.31%, +0.14%); it lost −0.48% a trade in the 2020 COVID crash. Found on 2020–2026 (+0.30% then +0.13% a trade). Not yet checked with the full deflated Sharpe. On paper since 2026-10-05: 36 trades, −0.096% a trade, 41.7% winners — a verdict needs 100 trades and 3 months (about early January 2027). One trade is about +0.2% on average and can lose several percent on a rally day; it works only over many trades. Real money on Zerodha only after a PASS.
NO TRADE — nothing on this tab has passed a test, so there is nothing here the desk can call a suggestion. Every rule tried on six years of NSE data failed (TRACK and the notes below have the numbers). The futures rows under the fold are untested ideas, scored on paper on TRACK. Watching them costs nothing; trading them is a guess. The FOCUS RULE above is the one exception under watch: it held on unseen data, and is on paper for GM only until its forward verdict.
UNTESTED — WATCH ONLY — 93 futures rows. Not a suggestion. Tap to see them.
If you take every row here (20 units each, before GM's charges): ₹35,85,252 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹53,775 — more if prices gap through the stops.
Most rows are in: Financial Services 16, Automobile and Auto Components 10, Healthcare 7. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend, a row's target comes before its stop at most as often as its break-even (about 37.5%) — a price with no trend is a fair game — so before GM's charges these rows make money only if the BUY signal works. It was tested and FAILED: the desk’s own rating, replayed day by day on six years of NSE’s own prices (2,36,746 stock-days), bought on this tab’s limit, target and stop, made −0.028% a trade after charges, 36.7% winners where 37.5% are needed (32,725 trades, t = −0.44).

1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 496 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹47,095 — ₹63,909 on average.

Results dates are NSE's own board-meeting filings, read 2026-10-16: 403 results meetings filed for the next 60 days. Companies must file at least two working days before the meeting (SEBI LODR Regulation 29), so “not announced” does not mean “no results”. Options whose results fall on or before their exit date are not listed (2339 contracts refused).

Calls — you BUY the call, it pays if the stock RISES

NO TRADE — nothing on this tab has passed a test, so there is nothing here the desk can call a suggestion. Every rule tried on six years of NSE data failed (TRACK and the notes below have the numbers). The call rows under the fold are untested ideas, scored on paper on TRACK. Watching them costs nothing; trading them is a guess.
UNTESTED — WATCH ONLY — 211 call rows. Not a suggestion. Tap to see them.
If you take every row here (one lot each): ₹25,27,403 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹13,10,741 — more if prices gap through the stops.
These 211 rows are on 46 stocks: several strikes of one stock are one bet, not several. Most rows are in: Financial Services 53, Automobile and Auto Components 33, Healthcare 30. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend and fairly priced options, a call is expected to lose about its charges: about −₹61,430.77 across all 211 rows, one lot each. 80 of 211 are priced above the stock’s own recent movement (implied above realised), which makes it worse. They make money only if the BUY signal works, and it failed: the desk’s own rating, replayed on six years of NSE’s prices, made −0.028% a trade on its BUY and ACCUMULATE rows (32,725 trades, 36.7% winners).
BAD-DAY RISK, every row together — 1 day in 20: −₹9,23,344 or worse · worst day: −₹21,63,554 · market opens 5% lower: −₹20,79,851
Today’s 211 rows (one lot each) replayed through each of the last 496 trading days, Wed, 16 Oct 2024 to Thu, 15 Oct 2026, on real prices, with every stop and target in the market. Not a forecast: these are days that already happened. Before charges.
1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 496 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹9,23,344 — ₹10,80,411 on average.
Worst day, Mon, 7 Apr 2025 (NIFTY −3.24%): 46 of 46 stocks fell and 211 stops were hit, 203 of them by a gap at the open — a loss of −₹21,63,554, against −₹12,63,088 if every stop had filled at its own price (before charges).
Market opens 5% lower: −₹20,79,851. Each stock opens lower by its own measured sensitivity to NIFTY (median 1.02), and a stop fills at the open, not at its own price.
Together: on those 25 worst days, 93.7% of the stocks fell at once. These rows are closer to one bet on the market than to 46 separate ones.
Most of the bad-day loss: OFSS 12%, LAURUSLABS 7.2%, DRREDDY 4%, MCX 4%, ADANIPORTS 3.5%.
Demergers, bonuses and splits are read from NSE’s own filings (Thu, 15 Oct 2026), so none of them counts as a crash.
For calls these figures are the pessimistic end. Each call is repriced with Black-76 at its own implied volatility, held where it is — and in a crash that volatility jumps, which cushions a call (India VIX moved +66% on Mon, 7 Apr 2025). By how much depends on each stock’s own option volatility, which this page has no history for.
Only on the stocks the desk rates BUY or ACCUMULATE — one side per stock, the side its analysis points to.

Every rule tried on six years of NSE data failed (TRACK and the notes below have the numbers). The put rows under the fold are untested ideas, scored on paper on TRACK. Watching them costs nothing; trading them is a guess.
UNTESTED — WATCH ONLY — 92 put rows. Not a suggestion. Tap to see them.
If you take every row here (one lot each): ₹15,81,714 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹8,20,268 — more if prices gap through the stops.
These 92 rows are on 24 stocks: several strikes of one stock are one bet, not several. Most rows are in: Capital Goods 28, Financial Services 14, Metals & Mining 11. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend and fairly priced options, a put is expected to lose about its charges: about −₹38,883.56 across all 92 rows, one lot each. 34 of 92 are priced above their own recent movement (implied above realised), which makes it worse. They make money only if the fall continues, and selling NIFTY in these downtrends failed its pre-registered test (final year t = 0.205).
BAD-DAY RISK, every row together — 1 day in 20: −₹5,58,800 or worse · worst day: −₹11,05,222 · market opens 5% higher: −₹12,61,107
Today’s 92 rows (one lot each) replayed through each of the last 496 trading days, Wed, 16 Oct 2024 to Thu, 15 Oct 2026, on real prices, with every stop and target in the market. Not a forecast: these are days that already happened. Before charges.
1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 496 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹5,58,800 — ₹7,08,754 on average.
Worst day, Tue, 3 Feb 2026 (NIFTY +2.55%): 24 of 24 names rose and 92 stops were hit, 80 of them by a gap at the open — a loss of −₹11,05,222, against −₹7,90,588 if every stop had filled at its own price (before charges).
Market opens 5% higher: −₹12,61,107. Each name opens higher by its own measured sensitivity to NIFTY (median 1.13), and a stop fills at the open, not at its own price.
Together: on those 25 worst days, 93.7% of the names rose at once. These rows are closer to one bet on the market than to 24 separate ones.
Most of the bad-day loss: CGPOWER 13.9%, CANBK 12.4%, ABB 7.9%, POWERINDIA 7.3%, LODHA 5.1%.
Demergers, bonuses and splits are read from NSE’s own filings (Thu, 15 Oct 2026), so none of them counts as a crash.
For puts these figures are the OPTIMISTIC end. Each put is repriced with Black-76 at its own implied volatility, held where it is — but a put loses on the days the market rises, and on those days implied volatility usually falls, which takes still more off a put (India VIX moved −7% on Tue, 3 Feb 2026). The real loss on such a day can be larger than shown.
The stock puts lean on the desk’s SELL and REDUCE ratings, and those were tested: shorting them LOST. Replayed on six years of NSE’s prices, shorting every SELL/REDUCE row on this desk’s limit, target and stop made −0.139% a trade (35,236 trades, t = −3.31 — reliably negative), and over 20 sessions those stocks did slightly BETTER than the market. INDUSTRY-ADJUSTED REVERSAL (long-short futures) — Every 5th session: buy the 10% of stocks that lagged their industry group most over the last 5 sessions, short the 10% that led it most; close both 5 sessions later. Industry = NSE's own filings, which give none for about a third of the 200 stocks; those are compared with each other as one group, exactly as in the backtest. Backtest: +0.15% a rebalance, t 1.98, 248 rebalances over 60 months — just short of the bar. COLLECTING — 1 finished, +0.145% a trade, 100% winners, worst 0.145%, t &mdash; (a verdict needs 26 rebalances).

FORWARD PAPER TEST: BORROWING SURGE (short futures) — When the shares out on loan in NSE's lending market (SLB) jump to at least 2x their 20-day average, and at least 1 lakh shares: short the stock at the open of the 2nd session after that day's file, cover at the close 5 sessions later. Backtest: +0.26% a trade over the market, 55% winners, t 2.23, 2,085 trades over 61 months (NSE data atlas study, 12 Oct 2026) — promising, not proven. Hit rate counts only trades that filled and then finished. IF RANDOM is how often the target would come before the stop if prices moved at random — each trade's break-even, before charges. Only a hit rate above it, over enough separate bets, is evidence of an edge. The touch odds the desk showed ignore the stop, so they always run higher. Futures returns are GROSS per unit; options are NET of every charge per lot. ALL has no average return (futures move about 1.5%, options about 50%), and its money is options net a lot plus futures at 20 units, gross.

HOW THIS IS SCORED. Every price this page freezes is bought on paper at the moment it is shown. Each build then checks the market, using the day’s high and low so a move between two builds is not missed. Every ambiguity counts against the record: a target and a stop in the same window is a stop; a target in the same window as the fill is not counted; a gap through the stop exits at the open; a fill is always at the limit, never better; a price from before the level was shown can never fill it. Unfilled day orders die at 15:30. Futures are held at most 20 sessions; options until expiry. Stored in the private repository under docs/ledger/, committed on every build, and copied to the Google Sheet.
WHERE THESE PRICES COME FROM. 303 priced from a live broker book, 0 from the 2026-10-15 settlement file. 303 of 303 options priced against the live futures price. Checked against NSE's own site at 2026-10-16 14:55 IST: 16 of 16 sampled contracts are the same contract on both (the same previous close), last prices within 4.58%. Broker login OK from the build server at 2026-10-16 14:54 IST — a NIFTY quote came back. F&O ban for 2026-10-16: AMBUJACEM, KAYNES, SAIL — left out entirely, because NSE allows only exits in a banned stock. This page is a snapshot, rebuilt on a schedule — it is not a live feed. Check the price on your broker before placing anything. Net figures are after brokerage, STT at 0.15%, exchange, stamp and GST; the spread is extra and is only known where a live book was seen.
NO SHOCK SHIELD. Nothing on this page stops buys on a bad global morning — not a GIFT Nifty gap, a crude or S&P move, or an India VIX spike. Those signals were tested on NSE’s own data and failed (or had too few events to test), so they do not gate anything. Check the market yourself before acting on a shock day.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. That any of it makes money. The paper ledger so far: futures 29 targets and 148 stops, 16.4% hit (95% range 6.1–26.6%); short futures 14 targets and 43 stops, 24.6% hit (95% range 11.5–37.6%); calls 228 targets and 704 stops, 24.5% hit (95% range 13.9–35%); puts 1002 targets and 924 stops, 52% hit (95% range 34.5–69.5%), over only 16 sessions of the same market. That says how this market went, not that a rule works — each row shows its own break-even. And every test fixed in advance so far, on data never used to build the rule, found no edge: the desk's own rating (replayed on six years of NSE data: −0.03% a trade on its buys, and its SELL/REDUCE shorts LOST −0.14% a trade, t = −3.3), 12-1 momentum, time-series momentum, low volatility, a 10-month market trend filter, and the NIFTY trend reader that now chooses between buys and puts (selling NIFTY in its downtrends: final year t = 0.21) — all six FAIL. The ranking is built on things that were measured, which is not the same as an edge that was proven. Size accordingly.
